authority: National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) / State Legal Services Authorities

description.en: Free legal aid for weaker sections of society under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987. Covers legal representation in courts, payment of court fees, preparation of legal documents, and advice on legal matters. Eligible persons include members of SC/ST communities, women, children, persons with disabilities, industrial workmen, persons in custody, victims of disasters, and persons whose annual income falls below the prescribed threshold. Applications are made through the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) or Taluk Legal Services Committee (TLSC).

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: Applicants belonging to Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe communities
verifiedConditions.claim: Members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes are entitled to free legal aid under Section 12(a) of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: Applicants whose annual income is below the prescribed threshold for the respective jurisdiction
verifiedConditions.claim: Persons whose annual income does not exceed the amount prescribed by the respective State Government are entitled to free legal services. The Supreme Court Legal Services Committee threshold and many state thresholds apply as notified.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: Women applicants seeking free legal aid
verifiedConditions.claim: Women and children are entitled to free legal services under Section 12(d) of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: Applicants with disabilities as defined under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
verifiedConditions.claim: Persons with disabilities as defined under the relevant disability legislation are entitled to free legal aid under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: Persons in custody including under-trial prisoners
verifiedConditions.claim: Persons in custody, including those in a protective home, jail, or mental health institution, are entitled to free legal services under Section 12(g) of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.

unverifiedEligibility: Victims of trafficking in human beings or beggars as referred to in Article 23 of the Constitution are eligible.
Victims of mass disasters, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake, or industrial disaster are eligible.
Industrial workmen are entitled to free legal aid for matters under specific labour legislations.
The income threshold varies significantly across states and is updated periodically by state notifications.
Children below 18 years are eligible regardless of income.

requirements.claim: A completed application form for free legal aid, available at the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) office or through the NALSA portal.
Proof of identity such as Aadhaar card, voter ID, or any government-issued photo identity document.

Income certificate or self-declaration of annual income is required when applying under the income-based eligibility criterion. Not required for applicants eligible under categorical criteria (SC/ST, women, disability, custody).

Documentary proof of eligibility category, such as caste certificate for SC/ST applicants, disability certificate for persons with disabilities, or custody certificate for persons in jail or protective home.
Details of the legal matter or case for which free legal aid is sought, including case number if already filed, court name, and brief facts of the case.

processInformation.appliesTo: All applicants seeking free legal aid
processInformation.claim: Approach the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) of the respective district, or the Taluk Legal Services Committee. Applications can also be submitted through the NALSA portal or by visiting Lok Adalat/legal aid clinics.

processInformation.appliesTo: All applicants seeking free legal aid
processInformation.claim: Submit the application form along with supporting documents to the DLSA. The application can be made in person, by post, or online through the NALSA portal where available.

processInformation.appliesTo: All applicants seeking free legal aid
processInformation.claim: The Secretary of the DLSA or the designated officer examines the application to determine eligibility under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
Upon confirmation of eligibility, a panel advocate is assigned to represent the applicant. The legal aid lawyer provides representation in the relevant court free of charge.
The DLSA monitors the progress of the case and ensures quality of legal representation. The applicant may request a change of advocate if not satisfied with the representation.

output.claim: Free legal representation by a panel advocate in courts at all levels (from subordinate courts to the Supreme Court). This includes payment of court fees, preparation and filing of legal documents, certified copies of judgments and orders, and any other expenses connected with litigation as deemed necessary by the Legal Services Authority.

fees.applicability: No fees are charged for legal aid applications or services
fees.claim: Free legal aid services are provided at no cost to the applicant. No application fee, court fee, or advocate fee is charged. All expenses of litigation are borne by the Legal Services Authority.

processingTime.applicability: From application to assignment of panel advocate, subject to completeness of documentation and eligibility verification
processingTime.claim: Applications for free legal aid are typically processed within 1 to 15 days from the date of submission. The DLSA Secretary is expected to dispose of applications expeditiously. In urgent matters such as arrests or custody cases, legal aid may be provided immediately.

sources.title: National Legal Services Authority — Official Portal

sources.evidenceExcerpt: NALSA provides free legal aid and advice to eligible persons through a network of State Legal Services Authorities, District Legal Services Authorities, and Taluk Legal Services Committees across India.
claimsSupported: Applications for free legal aid can be submitted through DLSA offices or the NALSA portal.
Required documents include identity proof, category proof, and case details.
Panel advocates are assigned to eligible applicants at no cost.
The DLSA monitors case progress and quality of representation.
No fees are charged for legal aid applications or services.
sources.uncertainty: Online application facility may not be available uniformly across all districts. Processing timelines depend on local DLSA workload.

sources.title: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
sources.publisher: Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 enumerates the persons entitled to free legal services: members of SC/ST, victims of trafficking, women and children, persons with mental illness or disability, persons in custody, victims of mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, industrial workmen, and persons whose annual income falls below the prescribed threshold.
claimsSupported: SC/ST members are entitled to free legal aid under Section 12(a).
Women and children are entitled to free legal services under Section 12(d).
Persons with disabilities are entitled to free legal aid.
Persons in custody are entitled to free legal services under Section 12(g).
Persons below the income threshold are entitled to free legal aid.
The DLSA Secretary assesses eligibility of applicants.
All litigation expenses are borne by the Legal Services Authority.
sources.uncertainty: Income thresholds are prescribed by respective state governments and vary across jurisdictions. The Act has been supplemented by various NALSA regulations and schemes.

limitations: This record covers free legal aid for individuals under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987. It does not cover legal aid provided by NGOs or private organizations.
The income threshold for eligibility varies across states and union territories and is updated periodically.
Online application facility may not be available in all districts; some DLSAs accept only in-person applications.
The quality and availability of panel advocates varies by district and is not modeled in this record.
Specific NALSA schemes for particular categories (e.g., victims of acid attacks, senior citizens, transgender persons) are not individually enumerated.
Lok Adalat and mediation services offered by Legal Services Authorities are not covered in this record.

review.reviewReason: Core eligibility criteria and process are reviewed based on the Legal Services Authorities Act and NALSA portal, but state-specific income thresholds and scheme-wise variations remain unmodeled.
